summary: This note is a clipped Wikipedia article about Teten Masduki, an Indonesian social activist linked to a public clearinghouse for information on corruption, collusion, and nepotism in Indonesia. It notes his 2005 Ramon Magsaysay Award, his appointment as Chief of Presidential Staff in September 2015, and his October 2019 appointment as Minister for Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises. The article is a stub and its text is under the CC BY-SA 4.0 license.
one_line: Indonesian social activist and anti-corruption figure who served as Chief of Presidential Staff and later as Minister for Cooperatives and SMEs.
key_facts: Teten Masduki was born on 6 May 1963 in Garut, Indonesia.
Teten Masduki is described as an Indonesian social activist involved in a public clearinghouse for information about corruption, collusion, and nepotism of Indonesia.
Teten Masduki was awarded the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2005.
Teten Masduki was appointed Minister for Cooperatives and Small and Medium Enterprises in the Onward Indonesia Cabinet in October 2019.
His ministerial term assumed office on 23 October 2019 under President Joko Widodo.
He was preceded as Minister for Cooperatives and SMEs by Anak Agung Gede Ngurah Puspayoga.
On 2 September 2015, Teten Masduki was appointed by President Joko Widodo as Chief of Presidential Staff, replacing Luhut Binsar Pandjaitan.
He served as Chief of Presidential Staff from 2 September 2015 to 17 January 2018.
He was succeeded as Chief of Presidential Staff by Moeldoko.
The article lists him as a Sundanese person and a Living person born in 1963.
A Tempo.co article dated 18 February 2013 reported that Teten Masduki launched a biography ahead of the elections.
He is listed as an ANSA-EAP Executive Committee Member.
The article is marked as a stub about an Indonesian activist and was last edited on 12 February 2024.
